messages:
Anya: seeing a sudden ECC/Xid spike across multiple zones, can anyone confirm?
Vik: yep alerts for us-west2 and eu-west1, error rate up ~6x, capacity shows ~12% GPU pool down.
Anya: confirmed from prometheus: gpu.ecc.errors{region=\"us-west2\"} jump at 1801233900. stack traces show lots of Xid 13/31 resets.
SRE-Bot: incident created: INC-2026-1801, severity P1. Pager sent to oncall.
Oncall: pinged, joining. Any signs of upstream network flaps or power events?
Sam-Ops: nothing in DC alerts. I can ssh a few affected hosts now.
Marta: I reproduced on a drained node: nvidia-smi shows ECC errors incrementing and GPU flapping in and out of CUDA driver.
Kevin: can we isolate by SKU? which GPU model?
Anya: majority are A100-40GB and a handful V100s in eu-west1. Same PCI bus errors in kernel logs.
Vik: running quick query: count by host of Xid errors -> top 7 hosts in us-west2, 3 in eu-west1.
Sam-Ops: running: for h in $(cat affected_hosts); do ssh $h 'dmesg | tail -n50 | grep -i pci\|nvidia'; done
Sam-Ops: results show repeated "NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:65:00): 31" and "NVRM: GPU has fallen off the bus".
Marta: that pattern suggests flaky PCIe link or thermal/power instability. Temps look normal.
Oncall: plan: 1) cordon + drain top hosts 2) failover workloads to other regions 3) vendor escalation for hardware replace. Agree?
Vik: agree. I'll kick off cordon for the top-7 and start live migration.
Anya: command to drain (we used):
```
kubectl cordon gpu-node-123
kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --force gpu-node-123
```
Marta: note: some pods have long-lived KV cache - we should add --grace-period=300 for controlled evictions.
Sam-Ops: doing rolling cordon now, marking nodes unschedulable in our inventory. Adding tags: "needs-hw-replace"
Infra-Bot: autoscaler triggered add-nodes in us-east1 (+10 GPUs) to maintain capacity.
Kevin: FYI that will spike spend; do we have headroom in committed pool?
Vik: we have reserved capacity in us-east1 but not enough for full failover, request temporary burst allowed.
Anya: product impacted: routed model requests show 8% increase in 500 errors during window. Alert to SLO owners sent.
Oncall: vendor ticket opened with logs and kernel traces, reference inc INC-2026-1801. Asking for priority swap of suspect cards.
Sam-Ops: gathered nvml logs and `nvidia-bug-report` from 5 hosts, uploaded to support bundle.
Marta: one oddity: some hosts recovered after a reboot, others didn't. Suspect intermittent PCIe link negotiation.
Vik: adding a mitigator: enable driver-level GPU reset throttle to reduce flapping, and expand retry timeouts in runtime. Rolling config via k8s daemonset.
Anya: pushed config; monitoring for reduced Xid rates.
SRE-Bot: update: incident severity remains P1. Current capacity impact: 9% across fleets.
Kevin: ops question: if vendor needs full card RMA, replacement route: repair vs swap at rack-level? cost/lead time?
Sam-Ops: vendor quoted 3-5 business days for RMAs, swap onsite recommended over shipping broken units back first.
Oncall: implement medium-term: drain + retag + move workloads out of affected racks. Long-term: consider replacing with redundant PCIe riser design on next procurement.
Marta: agreed. Also scheduling a focused test on risk hosts: stress PCIe link with `gpu_burn` + kernel logging to reproduce.
Vik: also enabled prefix caching fallback on runtime to avoid rehydration storms while nodes are drained.
Anya: SLO owners are notified; ETA for remediation: initial mitigation within 2 hours, vendor RMAs within 72 hours.
Infra-Bot: autoscaler scaled down + reclaimed healthy nodes; cost estimate for temporary burst ~ $4.8k/day (rough).
Kevin: flagging finance: temporary burst ok under emergency spend.
Oncall: status update to #incidents in 15m with current shard list and blocked pods.
SRE-Bot: next scheduled reminder in 30 minutes.
Marta: note for postmortem – add root-cause hypothesis: intermittent PCIe link negotiation under certain firmware combos + multi-socket power sequencing.
Anya: recording runbook steps we took into the incident doc: cordon/drain/topology tag/vendor bundle location/commands used.
Vik: I'll own the follow-up with procurement for procurement spec changes.
Sam-Ops: continuing drains, will post a short summary after the node list is finalized.
Oncall: thanks team. keep thread for coordination and paste dumps here. :thumbsup:
